verdict:
**1. The question, frozen.** What is explained: not the programme, but the draft's claims about this repository's record, and whether the draft and the making of the Workflow folder honour the repository's rules. Range: the draft W1 as it stands, the four older project folders, the five root files, and Semantics file 10 where the draft cites it. Asked: for each claim about a file, do that file's words bear it out (held), survive a nearer wording (loose), say otherwise (contradicts), or is nothing found (unknown); and for each rule, name it and put it beside the draft's sentence. Kind of question: *what counts as what under this rule* for Part B and C, *what can we tell from what we see* for Part A. Not asked, and not judged: whether the programme would work, whether the model is right, whether file 10 is true, whether a rival programme is better — the draft assigns those to other judges and I leave them there.

**2. The explanation in parts, and the jobs.** Parts, in the draft's own words: section 2's seven "what is fixed" bullets (the theory; the two skills; the other projects; who may run; the record; the evidence in hand; the reserve); section 3's three "why" paragraphs; the record-citing halves of M4, M6, M7 and M10; section 5's predictions P1.1 to P5; section 6's thirteen table rows and its "would count against the sketch"; sections 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13. Jobs: **J1 (given)** — the draft's own "Every claim below that uses a term of the theory quotes the sentence it rests on"; **J2 (given)** — the rules named in the task: one place per numbered file, nothing project-specific at the root, one project's folder only, predictions frozen first, the owner's word each phase, never Fable 5.1, Opus 5 geared at xhigh five at most, the other projects read only, keys in no file, raw evidence never edited; **J3 (given)** — section 12 asks nothing another project's conventions say must be done differently; **J4 (added by me)** — the section 6 table covers every operation of the dependence order it quotes, which is the draft's own falsifier, so adding it costs nothing; **J5 (added by me)** — every set Planning file 2 keeps apart is named: fitting, held-out, reserve. Parts held only by J4 or J5 would be *held if*; in the event both jobs are the record's own (section 6's falsifier line; Planning file 2 step 8), so nothing rests on me alone.

**3. Part by part.** Twenty-eight rows in the findings list, each with one mark and the holder quoted: eight *contradicts*, seventeen *loose*, one *held*, one *unknown*. No part idle: every bullet of section 2 and every prediction of section 5 does work that some other part does not, tested by removal. Provenance beside the marks: the record claims are *fitted* — drawn from files their writer had read before writing, which is why the two that are not (the reserve, and "no answer-keyed test has ever run") are the two that fail, both *asserted*, carried over from splits.md and H69 without a check against Language file 37. The rule claims are *built* where the draft quotes the rule and applies it (the owner's word before each phase, raw returns kept as they came, one project's folder, never Fable 5.1, Opus 5 at xhigh) and *asserted* where it names the rule and carries half of it (readers-and-markers; the key's second half). Headline: the load-bearing pair P3.2/P3.3 counts a field H64 struck as a count; phase 2 reads a held-out set H67 is still holding; the reserve is listed as clean when the record says fourteen of twenty-four are spent and three of ten are rewrites of the cases they were fitted on; "the first answer-keyed test in this repository" is contradicted by Language file 37; and the section 6 table fires the draft's own falsifier by leaving (O), (R), Deploy, (N), (G), (EK) and (U1)-(U3) out of the dependence order it quotes.

**4. (i) Name the three sets Planning file 2 keeps apart — fitting, held-out, reserve — with the 33 held-out sources and the spent fourteen Semantics cases in their right places, and freeze the split as its own numbered file before phase 2 runs; that one edit answers four of the eight contradicting findings. (ii) Replace every counted use of the same-explanation verdict with presence per document, as H67 did, or reword its criterion and record that as a new claim; P3.2 and P3.3 are the draft's load-bearing pair and cannot be read otherwise. (iii) Complete the section 6 table against the dependence order it quotes, so P4.1 has a denominator and (R) — which M4 rests on — has a holder.

**6. What this does not show.** Not that the programme is wrong: most of what I found is loose citation and missing sets, and loose is not wrong. Not that the model is right or wrong: I judged the record claims and the rules, not M1 to M10 as an explanation of LLM agents. Not that file 10 bears out the draft's theory claims: I read file 10 in full and checked the quotations I report on, and every one I checked is exact, but the sentence-by-sentence audit is another judge's task. Not that the eight contradicting findings are of one weight: the same-explanation field, the held-out set, the reserve and the answer-keyed claim bear on what phase 3 and phase 5 could conclude; the section 6 rows bear on one table. Not a score: the counts above are counts of quoted rows, not a verdict, and one missing set matters more than five loose citations.
